translation:
  text: '“The believers from the seventh mountain are like this. Its plants were green and cheerful, and
    the whole mountain flourished. Every kind of livestock and the birds of heaven grazed on the plants
    on this mountain, and the plants they grazed grew still more lush.”


    2. “They were always sincere, innocent and blessed, holding nothing against one another. They always
    rejoiced over God’s servants and were clothed in the holy spirit of these virgins.[a] They always
    had compassion for every person, and from their labors they provided for everyone without reproach
    or hesitation.”


    3. “When the Lord saw their sincerity and their complete childlike innocence,[b] he made them prosper
    in the work of their hands and granted them favor in all they did.”


    4. “I, the messenger of repentance, tell you who are like this: remain so, and your offspring will
    never be wiped out. For the Lord tested you and enrolled you in our number. All your offspring will
    dwell with the Son of God, for you have received from his spirit.[c]”'
  philosophy: optimal-equivalence
  footnotes:
  - marker: a
    reason: lexical_alternative
    text: The source links the singular holy spirit with the allegorical virgins. The house/clothing and
      virgins imagery is retained; lowercase presentation here does not decide a later doctrinal identification.
      Some letters in this phrase are restored in damaged Greek.
  - marker: b
    reason: textual_variant
    text: '“Childlike innocence” follows Gebhardt’s printed conjecture, compared with the two Latin traditions
      and9.29.1. Athos is reported as “gentleness”; Ethiopic is uncertain in the apparatus. Alternative:
      “When the Lord saw their sincerity and complete gentleness, he made them prosper in the work of
      their hands and granted them favor in all they did.”'
  - marker: c
    reason: textual_variant
    text: 'The final “spirit” is Anger’s printed conjecture, compared with Latin Vulgata, Palatina and
      Ethiopic. Athos is reported as “seed.” Alternative: “All your offspring will dwell with the Son
      of God, for you have received from his seed.” The object of “received” is unstated; neither fuller
      Greek agreement nor a specific theory of spiritual descent is claimed.'
